resources.string: Linux & Steam on Android — no root

WayLandIE needs Termux + a small Debian proot to run Linux / Steam games. Nothing here requires root. The wizard will walk you through each step, trigger it inside Termux for you, and then verify it succeeded.
Termux is the no-root Linux shell for Android. Tap below to open the Play Store / F-Droid entry, or install the APK from termux.dev.
Termux needs storage permission so WayLandIE can copy installer scripts into the shared Downloads folder. We will run `termux-setup-storage` for you.
Installs proot-distro, then `proot-distro install debian`. This pulls ~80 MB. No root needed — proot runs as a normal user.
Copies the WayLandIE linux-runtime installer scripts into ~/Downloads/WayLandIE so the Debian proot can see them.
Logs into the Debian proot and runs `sh install.sh --backend proot`. Installs Wayland, mesa, Vulkan loader, weston-simple-egl, gamescope.
Starts the bridge on the Android side so the Debian proot can connect to it. The display activity opens and shows the presenter surface.
Final sanity check: socket exists, Vulkan loader finds a driver, and a test render of vkcube completes. If doctor passes, you are ready.
Termux is not installed. Install it from F-Droid (termux.dev) and try again. The Play Store version is unmaintained.
Turnip (Mesa Vulkan for Adreno), DXVK (DirectX → Vulkan), and Qualcomm proprietary driver slots are managed inside Debian. Tap a slot to activate it for the next Steam launch.

WayLandIE preserves the original GPU-first zero-copy path:
Linux Wayland client (game / gamescope) → dmabuf fd → waylandie.display.bridge.v1 abstract socket → Android app imports the dmabuf as AHardwareBuffer via VK_ANDROID_external_memory_android_hardware_buffer → presented through SurfaceControl with USAGE_COMPOSITOR_OVERLAY.
No CPU copy on the hot path. proot does NOT break this because: • dmabuf fds are kernel-level; proot syscall translation does not affect SCM_RIGHTS fd passing. • Abstract sockets are not filesystem-based, so they work across proot. • AHardwareBuffer is an Android framework API; no root needed.
If `final-copy=forbidden` is set (default), the bridge will refuse to fall back to CPU-copy paths and will report an error instead of silently degrading.
